🚨 The truth behind Bruno Guimarães's move to Arsenal: how a beloved captain became "the enemy"
After four and a half years as a hugely popular figure at Newcastle, Bruno Guimarães returned to St James' Park as an opponent. The Telegraph reveals the story behind his £75M move to Arsenal in August and where he stands at his new club.

🎭 From "fury at Isak" to deciding to leave
Guimarães's pride was hurt in summer 2024 when his £100M release clause was not triggered. He was later made captain and shed tears after winning the Carabao Cup in March 2025. Last summer he was furious when Isak announced he wanted to join Liverpool, yet a year later he chose the same path. Turning 28 with his peak years limited, and feeling the club's project had hit a ceiling after Tonali and Gordon were sold, he left it to his agents to engineer his exit without getting his own hands dirty.

🇧🇷 Criticism in Brazil and Howe's departure
This summer's World Cup sealed his decision. He already felt Brazilian media undervalued him because he played for Newcastle, and after missing a penalty against Norway he took the blame for the early exit. That made him determined to test himself at a big club. Once Eddie Howe realised his captain's departure was unavoidable, he resigned, removing the last chance of Guimarães changing his mind.

💰 The mysterious "£45M offer" and the £75M deal
In July, a written "£45M offer" carrying the Arsenal logo was passed to Newcastle through an intermediary, but Arsenal stayed silent for weeks when Newcastle asked for confirmation. The document is believed to have been used to calm Guimarães, who was angry at the lack of progress, and to build pressure for a sale through the media. Direct talks between the clubs began at the end of July, and the move went through after Newcastle issued an ultimatum in early August: £75M in one payment, with no add-ons.

🔴 Arteta pushed it through as a "ready-made" signing
Some at the top of Arsenal had doubts about a £75M fee given his age of 29, a dip in his physical numbers last season and a serious hamstring injury earlier in the year. But Mikel Arteta led the push, arguing he was "a ready-made player worth at least 15 points a season." Partly due to managing his fitness, he has started only four of ten league games this season, but he has shown his big-moment quality by scoring winners off the bench against Sunderland and Leeds.

⚽️ From "exceptional" to "complacent": the "next step" Arteta took from the slump at Newcastle
The 2-2 draw at St James' Park showed two extreme sides of Arsenal. They dominated the first half and led 1-0 at the break, but after Mathias Jaissle's triple substitution lifted the home side, they conceded twice and needed Noni Madueke's equaliser to take a point home.

🎤 Arteta on "two points dropped" and the 96-minute standard
After the game Mikel Arteta said: "My feeling is that we dropped two points today. The first half was exceptional at every level, but we didn't make it 2-0, 3-0 or even 4-0." On the start of the second half he admitted: "When the opponent reacted, we were well below the standard required. We gave the ball away cheaply from a throw-in, conceded and gave them belief." He added: "Some players were at the top level for 70 minutes, but at this level that's not enough. Unless you score three or four and can ease off for 15 or 20 minutes, you have to compete for 96 minutes. That is the next step this team has to take."

👀 Redknapp and Wright on the "slack midfield"
The pundits were also critical of the second-half drop. Jamie Redknapp said: "Arsenal were just complacent in the second half. In the first half Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães had plenty of time, but once Jacob Ramsey came on they were closed down quickly, and Newcastle beat them on second balls and the basics of winning duels." Ian Wright said: "What worries me is the spell where they couldn't get control of the game back. I was really concerned by the Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães midfield. In that period they didn't look able to push the opponent back."

🔴 Madueke admits the "slack" and the champions' resilience
Noni Madueke, who equalised after Arsenal fell 2-1 behind, praised the team's "mental strength" but admitted about the start of the second half: "We didn't stick to our principles. Because the first half went well, maybe we went into the second half a bit too relaxed." Manchester City also dropped points on the same day, so Arsenal stay top, but together with David Raya's injury, the draw leaves the defending champions with work to do in their bid to retain the title.
